findings.claim: The VERSIONING.md 'Bad-tag recovery procedure' states: 'Adopters who pinned to the bad tag's SHA see the SCP-FRESH-001 warning on subsequent PRs (per ADOPT-001 §12.7.11) prompting them to bump.' This claim is technically accurate but operationally misleading: SCP-FRESH-001 fires only when the adopter's pin is more than 2 minor versions behind SCP main HEAD. If the bad tag is v1.1.0 and the corrected tag is v1.2.0, the warning will not fire until v1.4.0 is released (delta = 3 > freshness_warning_threshold_minor = 2). Non-Renovate adopters who manually SHA-pin face a detection window of potentially 3+ additional MINOR releases — weeks to months — before the freshness warning prompts a bump. The primary catch mechanism for the bad-tag scenario is Renovate's automatic bump PR (immediate for standard adopters per ADOPT-001 §12.7.2), not SCP-FRESH-001. The procedure does not disclose this distinction.
findings.evidence: VERSIONING.md 'Bad-tag recovery procedure' (lines 181–202): 'Adopters who pinned to the bad tag's SHA see the SCP-FRESH-001 warning on subsequent PRs (per ADOPT-001 §12.7.11) prompting them to bump.' ADOPT-001 §12.7.11: 'The SCP reusable workflow annotates ::warning::title=SCP-FRESH-001 on each PR run if your wrapper's pinned SHA is more than 2 minor versions behind the latest SCP release.' ADOPT-001 §12.7.11 warning condition: (main.minor - pinned.minor) > freshness_warning_threshold_minor (default 2). Concrete trace: bad tag = v1.1.0; corrected tag = v1.2.0; delta at v1.2.0 = 1 (no warning); delta at v1.3.0 = 2 (no warning); delta at v1.4.0 = 3 (warning fires). For non-Renovate adopters, SCP-FRESH-001 provides no signal until v1.4.0+. Renovate-based adopters (recommended path per ADOPT-001 §12.7.2) receive an automated bump PR to v1.2.0 immediately after the corrected tag is cut — this is the actual immediate catch mechanism.
findings.impact: Non-Renovate adopters (against best practice but possible) who SHA-pin to the bad tag remain on that SHA without machine-generated warning for the duration of 3+ subsequent MINOR releases. An operator reading the recovery procedure may believe SCP-FRESH-001 provides near-immediate detection for all adopter classes and therefore under-invest in manual notification (e.g. release-note urgency, direct adopter outreach). The bad tag's GitHub release note (per the procedure) provides a signal but relies on adopters watching the GitHub release feed. The real mitigation gap is that non-Renovate adopters have no timely machine-generated signal to bump past the bad tag.
findings.mitigation: Qualify the SCP-FRESH-001 claim in VERSIONING.md 'Bad-tag recovery procedure' to accurately describe the detection latency: 'Adopters using Renovate (ADOPT-001 §12.7.2 recommended path) will see an automated bump PR to the corrected v<X>.<Y+1>.0 within hours. Adopters who manually SHA-pin will see the SCP-FRESH-001 freshness warning only after 3+ subsequent MINOR releases elapse past the corrected tag (per the >2 minor threshold in §12.7.11). For manual-pin adopters, the release note on the bad tag's GitHub release page is the primary notification surface; consider adding a GitHub Security Advisory for adopters with policy-critical impact.' No code change to the workflow is required; this is a documentation accuracy fix in VERSIONING.md.

findings.claim: The dry-run pre-flight verification command documented in VERSIONING.md 'Tag-cut procedure' step 2 uses 'gh run list --workflow=release-gate.yml --limit 1' with the comment '# wait for completion + verify exit 0'. The gh CLI's 'run list' subcommand exits 0 regardless of the workflow run's conclusion (success, failure, or cancellation). The 'verify exit 0' comment refers to the workflow run's own conclusion (visible in tabular output) not the gh CLI process exit code — but the phrasing implies that checking '$?' after 'gh run list' would confirm the dry-run succeeded. A scripted operator who writes '[ $? -eq 0 ] && git push --tags' after the 'gh run list' invocation would silently pass even if the workflow failed. The human-operator path (reading tabular output) is not confused because the Status/Conclusion columns clearly show 'completed/failure'; the ambiguity affects scripted invocation only.
findings.evidence: VERSIONING.md 'Tag-cut procedure' step 2 (lines 174–178): 'gh workflow run release-gate.yml -f dry_run_tag=<tag>' followed by 'gh run list --workflow=release-gate.yml --limit 1   # wait for completion + verify exit 0'. The gh CLI documentation: 'run list' exits 0 on success of the CLI call itself, not of the listed workflow run. The correct command for scripted blocking-wait with exit code propagation is 'gh run watch <run-id>' (exits non-zero when the workflow fails) or 'gh run list --json conclusion --jq '.[0].conclusion'' checked against the string 'success'. The comment 'wait for completion' is also misleading: 'gh run list' does not block — it lists currently-known state and returns immediately. A human reading the output and waiting for 'completed' status is the implicit model, but this is not stated.
findings.impact: Operational annoyance and potential scripted misuse only. Human operators reading the tabular output would clearly see 'completed / failure' and know not to proceed. No direct security bypass surface — an operator who misreads the exit code and pushes a tag anyway would be caught by the post-tag observer (the last-line-of-defense path). The documentation gap weakens the operator's confidence in the dry-run verification step, which is the sole pre-emptive enforcement mechanism for CRIT-SAFE-001's closure.
findings.mitigation: Amend VERSIONING.md step 2 to document the wait-and-check idiom precisely: 'RUN_ID=$(gh run list --workflow=release-gate.yml --json databaseId --jq .[0].databaseId); gh run watch ${RUN_ID} --exit-status'. The '--exit-status' flag causes 'gh run watch' to exit non-zero when the workflow fails, making the scripted check correct. Alternatively note that 'gh run list' exits 0 always and the operator must inspect the 'conclusion' column for 'success' before proceeding. Either formulation removes the misleading 'verify exit 0' comment.

The '-warn' title variant is not separately registered. VERSIONING.md 'What does NOT count as breaking' (lines 93–94): 'Adding new informational ::warning:: or ::error:: titles (if existing titles preserved).' The SCP-EREL-001 row in §12.7.7 (line 980) describes two operating modes and mentions warning emissions in its narrative but does not define the '-warn' title variant as a separately searchable entry. findings.mitigation: Add a parenthetical to the SCP-EREL-001 row in ADOPT-001 §12.7.7 noting the '-warn' title variant: 'A non-blocking ::warning:: variant (title=SCP-EREL-001-warn) fires when an entry's announced_release is more than one major behind the candidate — operator advisory for potential backdating; does not block the tag-cut. Fires on SCP source repo only; adopter annotation parsers never receive this title.' This makes the registry complete without requiring a separate table row.

self_reported_concerns: CRIT-SAFE-001 closure: the architectural reframing is genuine. The workflow header, VERSIONING.md, and DISPATCH-NOTE now accurately state that the dry-run workflow_dispatch is the pre-emptive enforcement path and the push:tags trigger is a last-line-of-defense observer. The residual risk — that an operator can skip the dry-run — is honestly disclosed and consistent with the documented constraint. A stronger mechanism (requiring a workflow to pass before a tag-push is accepted) would require GitHub Repository Rulesets' 'Required workflows' feature, which is available only on GitHub Enterprise Cloud, not on personal accounts (jrnb2024/standards-control-plane- is a personal account on GitHub.com as of the review date). A feasible non-GHEC alternative is a wrapper script at scripts/cut-release.sh that enforces the sequence programmatically: trigger dry-run → block until gh run watch exits clean → push tag. This would close the documentation-only gap without requiring GHEC. Filing this observation as a self-reported concern rather than a finding because the existing documented constraint is explicitly acknowledged in VERSIONING.md and is consistent with v1.0.0 single-operator mode.

MAJ-SAFE-003 ORDERING INVARIANT verification: I verified the ordering in the actual CODEOWNERS file. '.scp/** @jrnb2024' is at line 71; '/CODEOWNERS @jrnb2024' is at line 83; 'docs/CODEOWNERS @jrnb2024' is at line 84. No entry after line 71 matches '.scp/**' paths. No entry before line 71 matches '.scp/**'. The ORDERING INVARIANT is preserved exactly as specified in the CODEOWNERS header comment. This closure is complete.

MAJ-SAFE-004 deprecation-ramp warning test verification: I traced the Python logic in release-gate.yml 'Check deprecation-ramp invariant' step exhaustively. The warning condition 'if ann_major < cand_major - 1' correctly produces: ann_major=1/cand_major=3 → 1 < 2 → TRUE (fires); ann_major=1/cand_major=2 → 1 < 1 → FALSE (doesn't fire); ann_major=1/cand_major=1 → 1 < 0 → FALSE (doesn't fire). Additionally: entries where ann_major < cand_major - 1 AND target == candidate get BOTH a warning AND a violation (the else branch of the major/same-major check fires because ann_major is neither == cand_major nor == cand_major-1). Double signal on the worst-case tamper path is a positive safety property.

TF-020H3rg-003 (auto-open issue) absence: the post-tag observer currently annotates the bad tag with SCP-EREL-001 and exits non-zero, but does not open a GitHub issue. At v1.0.0 single-operator mode, the operator who just pushed the tag would receive a GitHub Actions failure email and would be watching the Actions tab. The TF is appropriately tracked. The absence is not a new finding; it is an acknowledged limitation with a named tracked-forward item.

SCP-FRESH-001 adopter protection (R2-MIN-SAFE-001): Renovate-based adopters — the standard recommended path per ADOPT-001 §12.7.2 — are protected within hours of the corrected tag being cut via an automated bump PR. The MIN finding only affects non-Renovate adopters who manually SHA-pin, who are already operating against best practice. The documentation gap is real and should be fixed but does not represent a meaningful security failure in the recommended adopter configuration.

I did not find any new HMAC, flock, symlink, kernel-residency, or opt-in gate bypass surfaces introduced by fix-round-1. The fix-round-1 changes are bounded to: CODEOWNERS (one path addition), VERSIONING.md (three new subsections), workflow (five step modifications), ADOPT-001 (two table rows), STATUS.md (four edits). All new surfaces are documentation or annotation logic; no signing keys, no lock files, no kernel-level operations, no new external network calls were introduced.
